intro: The duty of candour is being open and honest with people about their care, especially when something has gone wrong.
points: Be open and honest whenever something goes wrong, telling the person the truth as soon as is reasonably practicable.
The statutory duty under Regulation 20, enforced by the CQC, sits with your organisation, not with you individually.
Your honest, prompt report is the foundation the whole formal process is built on, so never hide a mistake.
Give a truthful account, sticking to known facts; never guess, speculate about blame, or minimise what happened.
Saying sorry is right and expected; an apology is not, in itself, an admission of legal liability.
Report mistakes and near misses, and speak up; the law protects genuine whistleblowing in the public interest.
